title: "IPTW"
---

# Inverse probability of treatment weighting

IPTW balances treated and untreated groups on observed covariates by weighting each unit by the inverse of its probability of receiving the treatment it actually got. This module wraps `WeightIt` (weight construction) and `cobalt` (balance diagnostics).

The helper lives in [`R/iptw.R`](https://github.com/connectors-testing-pplx/research-paper-template/blob/main/R/iptw.R).

## 1. Estimate propensity scores and weights

```r
source("R/iptw.R")

iptw <- fit_iptw(
  data      = analysis_df,
  treatment = "treated",
  covariates = c("age", "sex", "educ", "income", "region"),
  method    = "ps",       # logistic propensity score
  estimand  = "ATE"      # or "ATT"
)
```

`fit_iptw()` returns the fitted weights and the propensity model. For a survey, pass `design = your_design` to weight the propensity model by sampling weights.

## 2. Diagnose balance

```r
bal <- check_balance(iptw, data = analysis_df, treatment = "treated")
print(bal)        # standardized mean differences before/after weighting
plot_balance(bal) # love plot -> outputs/figures/iptw-balance.png
```

Aim for standardized mean differences below 0.1 across covariates after weighting.

## 3. Trim extreme weights

Heavy tails inflate variance. The helper trims weights at a percentile you choose:

```r
iptw <- trim_weights(iptw, at = 0.99)
```

## 4. Estimate the treatment effect

```r
effect <- estimate_effect(
  iptw,
  data    = analysis_df,
  outcome = "y",
  family  = gaussian,
  design  = design,         # survey design for SEs
  cluster = "psu"
)
print(effect)   # weighted mean difference / risk difference with robust SE
```

The effect estimate uses a weighted outcome model with sandwich (or design-based) standard errors.

## Combined weights

When both sampling weights and IPTW weights apply, the final analysis weight is their product. The helper handles this internally when you pass `design`; downstream scripts simply use the combined weights saved to `data/processed/iptw_weights.parquet`.

## Where it plugs into the pipeline

`analysis/03-iptw.R` runs the four steps above and writes `iptw-balance.png` and `iptw-effects.csv` to `outputs/`.
